differences: Three visibly numbered Bandits now read as distinct combat targets rather than decorative silhouettes; each has an attached health bar and the selected target gains a restrained outline without disrupting the established 2.5D hierarchy.
The selected-enemy HUD pairs a concise encounter label and enemies-left count with the chosen enemy name and health, remaining readable at both supported iPhone sizes.
The damaged state clearly changes only Bandit Raider's attached bar and HUD value while the other two bars remain full, making independent health legible without adding a large roster panel.
The actors, health bars, and selection effects remain code-native structural combat artwork rather than production character/UI assets.
suggestions: Replace numbered structural silhouettes with approved enemy models, readable role silhouettes, target rings, and realm-specific health-bar materials while preserving per-enemy semantics.
Define authoritative encounter composition, spawn/despawn rules, enemy AI, aggro, damage, targeting, defeat, and reinforcements for player, Bandit, Gate, and Realm battles.
Move every enemy's health and defeated state plus final victory/reward validation to the authoritative battle service with prediction and reconnect reconciliation.
Add hit reactions, damage numbers, attack telegraphs, target-switch feedback, audio, haptics, and restrained effects with reduced-motion alternatives.
Validate touch target switching during simultaneous movement, longer localized enemy roles, color-independent damaged states, and VoiceOver traversal on physical iPhones.
reasoning: The battlefield now visually and behaviorally communicates a real multi-enemy encounter: all visible hostiles are selectable, attached bars expose independent health, the HUD identifies the active target and remaining count, and the compact layout remains uncluttered. The flow retains Another Life's established hierarchy and clears the visual threshold; remaining distance is production character, combat-feedback, and networking fidelity.
